eyebrow: Whole organization · ordinary unrestricted gift · SF, Bay and US health
program: Conditional value of a $100,000 unrestricted SFAF gift

nutshell.headline: An ordinary SFAF gift supports a broad portfolio; added overdose protection is its largest quantified health stream here.
nutshell.body: Central $2,018,525 per 10 SF QALYs for the whole gift, with 0.4954 SF QALYs per $100,000. Joint favorable assumptions yield $20,263, but are not a calibrated expected value or confidence bound. The earlier $56,328 figure applied only to hypothetical targeted naloxone spending.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: SFAF delivers overdose prevention and PrEP alongside HIV, HCV, behavioral health, housing and community support. Flexible funds may extend protection to people not reached by current funding.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Marginal allocations, unique-person reach, effect beyond existing rescue/PrEP access and available funding room remain unmeasured. Most portfolio costs are retained with their health unquantified.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No verified marginal unrestricted-gift budget or patient-linked additional-effect estimate. This replaces the scope of the organization estimate, not the historical program calculation or organization count.

summary.label: Central whole-gift donor cost /10 QALYs
summary.detail: Same $100,000 numerator; regional health is nested and never added.

summary.label: Explicit central allocation
summary.detail: Marginal judgments, not audited expense shares or a donor restriction. Full gift cost retained.

summary.label: Central associated resources
summary.detail: Includes unpriced outside medicine/lab/other resources. Gross envelope before funding replacement, not net social cost.

summary.label: Historical comparison
summary.detail: Legacy targeted-dose model remains inspectable. General giving cannot inherit that program allocation.

programSection.body: The audit spans sexual health, substance/behavioral care, linkage/retention/social support, policy, management and fundraising. Current services support two modeled mechanisms, not all measured organization benefit. The central allocation ledger also reserves 5% for HCV, 15% for HIV linkage/social support, 15% for other substance/behavioral health, 10% for other sexual/trans care, 5% for policy and 15% for central operations.

steps.title: Allocate the ordinary gift
steps.detail: $15,000 direct overdose support and$20,000 direct PrEP access; remaining$65,000 retained. Central operations are priced separately from branch direct unit costs.

steps.title: Reach distinct additional people
steps.detail: At $300 and $700 per offer, the gift supports 50 overdose-response and 28.57 PrEP offers. Allowing for replacement of existing funding reduces these to 20 overdose-response participants and 8.57 PrEP offers. Assuming 90% of PrEP recipients are distinct from the overdose-response group leaves 7.71 people credited with PrEP benefits.

steps.title: Compare two finite trajectories
steps.detail: Recurring overdose rescues affect one person's survival curve. PrEP changes finite time without HIV, allowing later infections in both arms.

steps.title: Deduplicate and value health
steps.detail: No new lifetime per reported reversal. Exclude overlap from PrEP gains; retain its costs/harms. No extra HCV/MOUD survival, transmission or other portfolio health added.

programSection.boundary: Neither a dose, a training nor a PrEP prescription is a causal life saved. All quantities beyond service existence are scenario inputs.

model.headline: Whole gift, unique cohorts and finite clinical benefits
model.body: Central overdose survival contributes 0.508789 US QALYs and disjoint PrEP morbidity 0.016082, before regional allocation. Both benefits compare actual available care with finite added protection. Death and infection remain possible after support ends.

equation.label: Finite-state whole-gift bridge
equation.expression: Unique people = gift × branch allocation / direct offer cost × financing additionality (× disjoint fraction for PrEP). OD benefit integrates supported survival minus baseline survival. PrEP benefit integrates supported HIV-free survival minus baseline HIV-free survival × treated-HIV utility gap. Subtract distinct present-valued harms. Whole-gift price = 10 × gift / regional net Q.
equation.result: US 0.524871; Bay 0.518979; SF 0.495411 QALYs. SF donor $2,018,525 / gross associated resources $2,791,332 per 10 QALYs.

inputs.label: OD /PrEP gift allocation
inputs.basis: Audit establishes portfolio breadth, not next-gift shares. Central other 65% priced but unquantified. Funding additionality does not stand in for allocation.

inputs.label: Direct cash per supported offer
inputs.basis: Includes recruitment failures, branch staff, follow-up and program administration. Central corporate management/fundraising is in separate 15% retained spending. Outside medication/lab inputs priced separately.

inputs.label: Financing additionality
inputs.basis: Existing government support, assistance, 340B operations and other donors stay baseline. Does not measure clinical change or unrestricted allocation.

inputs.label: Recurrent events /fatality without effective rescue
inputs.basis: External Medicaid recurrence and mortality inform scale only. Events can recur in survivors; fatal hazard is event rate × untreated fatality × failure of effective rescue.

inputs.label: Effective rescue baseline /increment
inputs.basis: Includes witness access, timely dosing, EMS and alternative rescue. It is not the pharmacological reversal rate or reported reversals/doses.

inputs.label: OD protection /finite survival
inputs.basis: Baseline fatal hazard totals .07 centrally. The .06 hazard excludes overdose death already modeled. Following support both arms return to baseline risk; survival difference is integrated once.

inputs.label: PrEP baseline HIV hazard /additional effective coverage
inputs.basis: PROUD's 86% relative effect is an external active-PrEP scale. Its much higher control incidence is not imported. Coverage increment is added protected time beyond actual care.

inputs.label: PrEP support /finite morbidity
inputs.basis: Common mortality .01 and later infection continue. Gap compares HIV-free with treated HIV, not untreated AIDS; no HIV mortality/transmission credit. Not direct SFAF utility evidence.

inputs.label: Disjoint PrEP health fraction
inputs.basis: Excludes people/person-time already credited under overdose survival. Full PrEP costs and harms remain; no added MOUD/HCV tail on those same survivors.

inputs.label: Outside resources per nominal offer
inputs.range: Donor-pays sensitivity moves these into direct cash
inputs.basis: Medication/lab/other real inputs outside branch cash and corporate overhead. Not insurance transfers or 340B revenue. Assumes associated inputs before replacement; no savings subtraction.

inputs.label: OD Bay/SF;PrEP Bay/SF
inputs.range: Favorable PrEP SF 85%; zero SF case
inputs.basis: SF nests within Bay. Shares include mobility over health horizon; service-site location alone does not prove residence.

inputs.label: Shared /independent loss
inputs.range: .04 OD /.01 PrEP per incremental offer;.1 independent QALY
inputs.basis: Already gift-date PV, no extra discount. PrEP shared harm applies even to overlap-excluded people; independent harm survives zero funded activity.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: The central value is a judgmental partial-health best estimate for the whole gift. Joint favorable inputs are not a confidence bound or high-expected-value claim. Null and harm cases retain gift costs. Shorter protection and health horizons can substantially worsen value; new recurring risk can increase both need and survivor attrition.
model.fundingBoundary: May 2026 contract request remains conditional on appropriations; June partial restorations do not resolve the current Pick Up Crew gap. Public PrEP benefits and 340B operations remain baseline. Liquid assets do not establish spare cash or absence of need. Verified funding room remains null.

evidence.result: Multiple clinical/support/policy functions plus central operations are present.
evidence.transfer: Historical expense categories guide breadth; none is a verified marginal gift share.

evidence.result: Repeated overdose and subsequent fatal overdose are observed.
evidence.transfer: A recurrent-event survival model is warranted, but current SFAF event/rescue hazards remain priors.

evidence.design: PROUD randomized immediate versus deferred PrEP
evidence.result: 86% relative acquisition reduction; substantial background incidence.
evidence.transfer: Neither local incidence, added access, utility gap nor funding additionality is supplied by this trial.

evidence.population: SFAF programs and eligible PrEP clients
evidence.result: Existing public and assistance routes support care.
evidence.transfer: They neither prove every client is reached nor identify a priced unfunded cohort.

reservations: Most whole-organization health remains unquantified; retained cost is not evidence those services lack value.
Unique-person costs and recurrence/rescue hazards are unmeasured, replacing the old repeated-report shortcut with an explicit prior-based survival comparison.
PrEP morbidity utility is an assumption; no direct patient utility, secondary transmission or mortality advantage is credited.
Current spending authority, additional staff/medicine supply and final public cuts/restorations remain unverified.
Combine models only after person-level deduplication with HYA, GLIDE, HRTC, SFPHF, clinical partners and other funded providers.
excludedBenefits: HCV cure and HIV linkage/retention benefits
MOUD, other behavioral health and drug-use morbidity
Housing, food, community support and trans/sexual health beyond PrEP
HIV mortality and secondary transmission prevention
Policy, statewide appropriations and broader welfare
Nonfatal overdose brain-injury prevention and health beyond finite horizons
